newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: RESEARCH ALERT-Manila stocks fears said baseless.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Manila stocks fears said baseless.

text.p: Peregrine Securities Philippines Inc said on Friday fears that Philippine banks could be affected because of exposure to the property sector were "groundless."
Peregrine in a report to clients also rejected a view expressed by another brokerage that corporate results would be poor.

"We find it difficult to conclude corporate performance will be dismal given economic conditions within which companies will be operating are more favourable now than they were last year, indeed in a long time," Peregrine said.
"Instead of heading for the exit, investors should be looking to pick up attractively priced issues which are also not vulnerable to the prevailing negative sentiment," it said.

Philippine property stocks had been hit hard in the past few days due to fears of a reported glut in office and condominium space. The slide affected some banking stocks as well on talk some banks had large loan exposures to the property sector.

But Peregrine's chief economist Luz Lorenzo said among other stocks she was recommending a buy on Ayala Land, one of the biggest property firms in the country. She also recommended a buy on Metropolitan Bank and Trust Inc.

"Vacancy rates, which are a leading indicator of the viability of loans to property developers/investors, are not worrying ... Given the indicators, it is unlikely property prices will collapse," the report said.
Other stocks recommended as buys by Peregrine were Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co, Manila Eletric Co, retailer SM Prime, construction firm DMCI Inc and electronics firm Solid Group.
